Not being an American, I'm honestly curious.... Is it true that the tuition tax credit mainly only benefits "relatively affluent families"?

In my experience, not exactly. I make about $23,000 a year as a graduate student, and this is what I remember from doing my taxes this year.

To apply tuition expenses to your tax return, you can choose one of two options. The first, and what I did, is to deduct your expenses from your adjusted gross income (AGI), which is then used to calculate how much tax you owe. If you make under something like $60,000 a year, you can deduct up to $2000. Otherwise, up to $4000. For me, making $23,000, a $2000 deduction from my AGI added another $200 or so to my tax return (the money I received back from the government).

The other option is to choose one of two credits which are applied after your owed tax has been calculated. I don't remember the names of the credits, so I'll call them credit A and credit B. Credit A didn't apply to me because it is only for undergraduates, but it looked like it could reduce your taxes a good amount. If the wealthy are better off with tuition tax credits, this is probably the source. The other credit, credit B, does apply to graduate students, but it's a piece of shit. It can only reduce the amount of money you have to pay to the government (if the taxes you paid out of your paycheck throughout the year are less than the tax you owe), but it cannot increase the amount of money you receive back from the government if you overpaid throughout the year.

Now, of course, I used what I'll call the advanced poor/middle class tax form, the 1040A. The easiest tax form, aimed at the poor, is the 1040EZ (yes, as in "easy"), and while it offers the credits (option 2), it does not mention the AGI reduction (option 1), which is the better option (at least for graduate students). This is one way the poor are fucked over. I did not look at any of the tax forms for wealthier people, so maybe there are additional tuition tax credits they can benefit from that I don't know about.
